newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Edegel negotiates three supply contracts.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Edegel negotiates three supply contracts.

text.p: Electricity firm Edegel aims to sign three major supply deals with local companies, including Peru's top steel-maker, to add to its $450 million accord with Cominco Ltd, an official said late Tuesday.

Edegel's general manager Pedro Pablo Errazuriz told Reuters in a telephone interview he hoped to finalize two of the new contracts next week as the utility aimed to make its client portfolio more balanced.

One of the supply contracts would be with Empresa Siderurgica del Peru -- the country's largest producer of steel with a 400,000 tonne a year capacity, Errazuriz said, without giving more details of the agreements.
Electricity distributors Luz del Sur and Edelnor receive more than 90 percent of Edegel's roughly 520 megawatts (MW) of energy supply, the official said.
But Edegel -- with an installed capacity to generate 825 MW -- aims to balance evenly its supply between the distributors and firms outside of the electricity industry, Errazuriz said.

Edegel, Peru's top private generator and a blue chip stock on the Lima bolsa, improved this balance when it announced earlier Tuesday a deal locking Cominco into a 15-year contract to receive electricity for its Cajamarquilla zinc refinery.
"The signing of that contract is the largest we have made with a 'free' (non-electricity sector) client," Errazuriz said.
